title: 4 · Lock-Based Protocols & Deadlock (Unit 3)
learn:
Locks

A lock gives a transaction exclusive use of a data item. Shared lock (S): read only. Exclusive lock (X): read and write. Compatibility: S with S is allowed; S with X, X with S and X with X are not. Any number of transactions can hold S, but only one can hold X. Upgrading turns S into X; downgrading turns X into S.

Problem with simple locking

A=1000, B=500. T1 locks A, subtracts 100, unlocks A early. T2 reads A=900 and B=500 (total 1400) before T1 adds 100 to B. The correct total is 1500, so the result is inconsistent.

Two-phase locking (2PL)

All lock operations precede all unlock operations. Growing phase: acquire locks only. Lock point: the final lock. Shrinking phase: release only. 2PL guarantees serializability but may reduce concurrency (holding locks unnecessarily, locking too early) and can deadlock.

Variations

Conservative (static) 2PL: take all locks before starting, release after commit; deadlock free. Strict 2PL: X locks held until commit or abort; gives cascadeless schedules. Rigorous 2PL: all locks held until commit; avoids cascading rollback. Strict and rigorous can still deadlock.

Deadlock

Two or more transactions each wait for a lock held by another. Detect it with a wait-for graph: node per transaction, edge Ti → Tj when Ti waits for an item held by Tj. A cycle means deadlock. Four necessary conditions: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, circular wait.

quiz.q: In 2PL, after the first unlock the transaction may?

quiz.why: All locks are taken up front.

quiz.q: A cycle in the wait-for graph means?
quiz.why: Everyone in the cycle is stuck.

quiz.q: Which is NOT a necessary condition for deadlock?
Strict 2PL holds which locks until commit/abort?

lab.task: T1 holds X(P) and waits for Q; T2 holds X(Q) and waits for P. Draw the wait-for graph and name the problem and one way to prevent it.
lab.solution: Edges T1→T2 and T2→T1 form a cycle: deadlock. Prevent with conservative 2PL (lock everything first) or a global lock ordering (break circular wait).
